doc: The standing offers — world v129. The authored half of drama.json §51 bounded_opportunities and the jobs-housing counterpart to crowd.json occasions: concrete, bounded invitations anchored at every door venue and every registry building. Each offer names a host (who keeps it legible — a person, staff, the house, or the regulars), a cost in time/stuff/game-dollars, a capacity, a cadence, a changes line (the readable consequence IF taken up) and a neglect line (the honest decay state if ignored). CONDITIONS, NEVER SCRIPTS — uptake belongs to the characters; an ignored offer is texture, not a fuse, and nobody tracks attendance. INTERNAL tier for machine surfaces; board-visibility offers are the only spectator-legible rows.

kind_keys.shared_workspace: a bench, stove, shelf, line, or lift anyone may use on the house's terms — the space is the offer
kind_keys.open_invitation: a standing ask that repeats — a table, a sign-up sheet, a night, a jar; join by showing up
kind_keys.community_project: a named ongoing effort with a physical trace — a garden bed, a shelf, a fund jar; it persists whether or not anyone shows

visibility_keys.board: posted where anyone can read it — spectator-legible
visibility_keys.counter: staff-side or regulars-side knowledge — internal and staff contexts only
visibility_keys.quiet: household or handshake knowledge — internal only, redacted below internal clearance

host_forms.person: a cast/supporting/ambient id (c1–c8, s1–s3, a01–a20) — the person who keeps the offer legible; may let it lapse
host_forms.staff: the venue collectively — whoever is behind the counter that day
host_forms.house: the household — no single keeper; the offer lives in the shared space itself
host_forms.regulars: the regulars — kept alive by habit, not by a named keeper

mudhaus.ask: Claim a month on the art wall — bring six to ten pieces, hang them yourself on the first Sunday, leave a price card only if you want one.

cost.bring: your own work and your own tape

mudhaus.capacity: one wall, one artist a month
mudhaus.since: since the second year — a regular asked to hang her sketches and Marisol said the wall was wasting light anyway
mudhaus.changes: a wall-month makes the artist a known face at the counter — regulars start asking what's next, and the clipboard name gets recognized on the street
mudhaus.neglect: the clipboard stays taped up with blank months; last year's show hangs three months too long and fades at the corners

mudhaus.ask: The community shelf — leave a book, take a book, tuck a flyer on the cork edge if it's for something on the block.

cost.time: none — a minute at the shelf
cost.bring: a book you'd actually hand someone

mudhaus.capacity: one shelf; when it overflows the overflow goes to the Dusty Spine
mudhaus.since: since forever — nobody remembers who left the first book
mudhaus.changes: the shelf is how a flyer for a balcony show or a lost cat actually travels — a thing posted here gets seen by everyone who waits for a latte
mudhaus.neglect: the shelf fills with water-damaged paperbacks nobody wants and the cork edge goes blank — Jules or Dani weeds it when it embarrasses them

el-farolote.ask: The Thursday table — one long table stays unreserved on Thursdays; ask by Wednesday and a seat gets set, family-meal price, no questions about who you came with.

cost.time: a long dinner — the table eats slow
cost.bring: nothing; an appetite is the ticket

el-farolote.capacity: the table seats ten; it has never once filled
el-farolote.since: since Tomás started running the pass — staff meal kept having extra seats and it felt wrong to waste them
el-farolote.changes: a seat at the Thursday table turns a neighbor into a regular — Tomás learns your order, and the kitchen starts saving you the good salsa
el-farolote.neglect: the table sits with ten empty chairs some Thursdays and the staff eats at it instead — nobody takes it personally, nobody writes it down

el-farolote.ask: The prep stool — Sunday mornings, whoever shows gets a cutting board and a pile of something to break down; you eat the family meal after.

cost.bring: nothing — the knives are the house's

el-farolote.capacity: two stools, three if someone doesn't mind the small board
el-farolote.since: since a regular's kid needed to learn knife work for a job interview and stayed a year
el-farolote.changes: a stool regular picks up real knife skills and a kitchen reference — and the family meal stops feeling like charity because they cooked it
el-farolote.neglect: the stools stack in the corner and Tomás preps alone with the radio — the offer stays open but the pile gets smaller

auerbach.ask: The Tuesday bench — bring the broken thing and the part if you know it; Victor supervises, you do the work, the shop's tools do the rest.

cost.bring: the broken thing; the part if it's exotic

auerbach.capacity: one bench, one project — the queue is the line of things on the floor
auerbach.since: since 2009 — a customer asked if Victor fixed toasters and he said 'no, but I'll watch you do it'
auerbach.changes: a bench regular stops paying repair shops and starts being the person other people bring toasters to — competence the block can see
auerbach.neglect: the bench holds the shop's own backlog and the sign goes face-down for a season — nobody un-offers it, it just waits

auerbach.ask: The stoop fund jar — coins and small bills toward the sidewalk planter rebuild; when the jar covers lumber, a Saturday gets named and whoever shows builds it.

cost.time: a Saturday if the jar ever fills
cost.bring: coins, or hands on build day

auerbach.capacity: one jar, one planter, whoever's there
auerbach.cadence: standing — the jar fills at its own pace
auerbach.since: since the delivery truck clipped the planter and Victor decided the fix belonged to the block
auerbach.changes: a filled jar becomes a named Saturday — sawdust on the sidewalk, coffee appearing from somewhere, and a planter everyone watched get built
auerbach.neglect: the jar sits at two coins and a button for months; the chipped planter stays chipped and the jar reads as a wish, not a plan

dolores-perk.ask: The patio pitcher — bus the outside tables on your way out and your refill is on the house; the little chalkboard by the door explains it once, forever.

cost.bring: nothing

dolores-perk.capacity: as many as want it — the tub lives under the side counter
dolores-perk.since: since the summer the park crowd kept leaving cups and a regular cleared them without being asked
dolores-perk.changes: a habitual table-clearer gets remembered by name at the register — the smallest job on the block with the fastest promotion to regular
dolores-perk.neglect: the chalkboard fades, the tub migrates behind the counter, and the offer quietly becomes staff-side knowledge only

buy-rite-market.ask: The Saturday sample table — local makers get the folding table by the door for two hours; sign up on the clipboard at register two, bring your own tablecloth.

cost.bring: samples, a tablecloth, a card with your name

buy-rite-market.capacity: one table, one maker per Saturday
buy-rite-market.since: since the hot-sauce guy outsold the shelf stock from a card table and the manager made it official
buy-rite-market.changes: a good Saturday puts a maker's name in fifty kitchens — the clipboard is the cheapest shelf space in the neighborhood
buy-rite-market.neglect: the clipboard goes a month blank and the folding table stays in the back — the slot exists but the block forgets to use it

buy-rite-creamery.ask: The flavor chalkboard — write a flavor suggestion in the chalk column; the staff pick each month gets made as a pint special and the suggester gets the first scoop free.

cost.bring: a flavor that isn't a joke — the staff can tell

buy-rite-creamery.capacity: the column holds about twenty lines before it gets erased and started over
buy-rite-creamery.since: since the ube-and-everything month proved the customers had better ideas than the catalog
buy-rite-creamery.changes: a winning flavor makes a name briefly famous on the block — 'the pretzel one was mine' is a real claim people make
buy-rite-creamery.neglect: the column fills with the same three jokes and the staff stops reading it — the chalk stays up but the pick quietly stops

il-delfino.ask: The industry stool — service workers from anywhere on the block get the end bar stool after close and a staff-priced plate; say where you work, that's the whole ticket.

cost.bring: the name of your shift

il-delfino.capacity: two stools — more would turn it into a seating section and it isn't one
il-delfino.since: since a Farolote cook came in still wearing his apron and nobody made him change
il-delfino.changes: the stool is how the block's kitchen crews actually meet each other — a cook's gossip network two seats wide
il-delfino.neglect: the stools get taken by walk-ins on busy nights and the tradition goes quiet until a bartender remembers to defend it

baguette-about-it.ask: The four a.m. bench — the bench by the oven vent is warm before dawn; early workers and insomniacs can sit with a paper cup while the first proof comes up, as long as they don't block the flour run.

cost.time: the cold hour before the city starts
cost.bring: nothing — Hana sets out the day-olds when there are some

baguette-about-it.since: since Hana noticed the same nurse's-aide waiting for the first bus in the cold and unlocked the door early
baguette-about-it.changes: a bench regular has a warm hour and a known face at the loneliest part of the day — the bakery's first fifteen minutes become a small community
baguette-about-it.neglect: the bench sits cold in the dark when Hana's schedule shifts — the door stays locked and nobody thinks to ask

baguette-about-it.ask: The proofing lesson — Hana will teach one person at a time to shape loaves on Sunday afternoons; the deal is you take your misshapen results home and eat them.

cost.time: three Sunday afternoons to be any good
cost.bring: an apron and humility

baguette-about-it.capacity: one learner at a time — two hands at the bench is a crowd
baguette-about-it.cadence: sunday afternoons, when Hana's week allows
baguette-about-it.since: since a counter kid asked why her baguettes stood up straight and got a real answer
baguette-about-it.changes: a learner leaves with a working skill and a standing invitation — and Hana gets the only thing a 4 a.m. baker can't buy: company that understands the hours
baguette-about-it.neglect: nobody's asked in a year — the Sunday bench does baguettes for the case and the lesson exists only because it was never withdrawn

the-600-club.ask: The league sheet — the pool league takes walk-ons for the Monday open bracket; put your initials on the sheet, bring your own cue or borrow the warped one, lose gracefully at least once.

cost.bring: a cue if you have one; the buy-in covers the table light

the-600-club.capacity: sixteen initials; the sheet rarely fills
the-600-club.since: since the regular league died of attendance and the open bracket replaced it — less glory, more strangers
the-600-club.changes: a walk-on who keeps showing up becomes a Tuesday regular who happens to play Mondays — the sheet is the club's only recruiting tool
the-600-club.neglect: the sheet hangs with five faded initials for weeks and the table plays winner-stays like always

dandy-lion.ask: The tempering watch — first Saturday of the month the marble slab runs a tempering demo; stand at the rail, ask questions, take the tasting spoon when it comes around.

cost.bring: nothing — questions are optional, patience isn't

dandy-lion.capacity: the rail holds six before sightlines go
dandy-lion.since: since a customer asked why the chocolate snapped and got a forty-minute answer the whole shop enjoyed
dandy-lion.changes: a rail regular starts recognizing temper by eye and gets pulled into tastings — the demo makes connoisseurs out of neighbors
dandy-lion.neglect: the demo skips a month when the kitchen's slammed and nobody complains — the sign's date just quietly updates

valencia-growers.ask: The cull crate — at close, the crate by the scale holds the day's too-soft and too-ugly; help break down empty boxes for ten minutes and the crate is yours to pick through first.

cost.time: ten minutes of breaking down boxes at close
cost.bring: a bag — the crate never comes with one

valencia-growers.capacity: whoever's there at close; the crate feeds three honest pickers
valencia-growers.since: since the compost run started costing more than the produce was worth and the closing crew found the better math
valencia-growers.changes: a cull regular eats well on a thin week and becomes the person the closing crew watches for — interdependence measured in soft tomatoes
valencia-growers.neglect: the crate goes to compost unclaimed some nights — the offer stays taped to the scale whether or not anyone reads it

needlepointe.ask: The apprentice hours — one evening a week the shop takes small flash work at apprentice rates while Bex builds her book; you pick from the posted sheet, you tip what the piece is worth to you.

cost.bring: a shower and a decision

needlepointe.capacity: one chair — the shop's books, not the offer, decide the wait
needlepointe.since: since Bex's apprenticeship needed skin hours the shop's regulars couldn't all supply
needlepointe.changes: the hours make Bex's line-work visible on the block — every healed piece is a walking reference, and her book gets thick in public
needlepointe.neglect: a slow month leaves the sheet unbooked and Bex practices on skin sheets instead — nobody's disappointed, it just shows in the pace

folsom-auto.ask: The Sunday bay — when the shop's closed Gus opens one lift for do-it-yourself work; you bring the oil and the filter, he supervises from the stool, and you leave the bay cleaner than you found it.

cost.bring: your own oil, filter, and the willingness to do it yourself

folsom-auto.capacity: one lift, first ask gets it
folsom-auto.cadence: sundays, when Gus feels like opening
folsom-auto.since: since Gus got tired of watching neighbors overpay for oil changes he could supervise for free
folsom-auto.changes: a bay regular learns their own truck — the block gets one more person who can tell a bad belt by sound
folsom-auto.neglect: the bay stays closed the Sundays Gus fishes — the offer's rhythm is his weekends and everyone knows it

maliks.ask: The cork board — the wall by the door takes flyers for anything real on the block: room shares, lost cats, lessons, the church basement sale. Pushpin it yourself; Malik clears it the first of the month.

cost.bring: a flyer small enough to leave neighbors room

maliks.capacity: the board holds maybe thirty before it's wallpaper
maliks.since: since the first lost-dog flyer worked and word got around that the board actually gets read
maliks.changes: the board is the block's slow internet — a room share posted here finds a tenant through three conversations instead of an algorithm
maliks.neglect: the board goes a month of stale flyers and dead dates — Malik's first-of-the-month clearing is the only curation it gets

las-palmas.ask: The tarp pull — when the marine layer comes in wet, whoever's standing there helps Luz pull the tarp and stack the crates; the deal is the soft-fruit bag at the end.

cost.time: fifteen minutes of fast work at exactly the wrong moment
cost.bring: dry hands and luck

las-palmas.capacity: two helpers is plenty; three is a traffic jam
las-palmas.cadence: whenever the weather turns — no schedule, all sky
las-palmas.since: since the first storm Luz weathered alone and the stand's regulars watched it happen
las-palmas.changes: a tarp-pull regular becomes someone Luz feeds in soft mangoes and remembers by name — help at the hard minute buys more than a polite hour does
las-palmas.neglect: the tarp gets pulled alone on the wet days nobody's around — the stand survives, the offer just goes unanswered

bloom-and-doom.ask: The stem bucket — day-old stems go in the bucket by the door after five; take a bunch, leave the bucket, and if the bunch is for somebody sick Ida will tell you which stems hold up.

cost.bring: a jar at home — the stems don't come with one

bloom-and-doom.capacity: one bucket; it empties most days by six
bloom-and-doom.since: since Ida decided composting perfect stems was a sin the shop didn't have to commit
bloom-and-doom.changes: the bucket makes half the block's kitchens smell like flowers for free — and Ida learns who in the neighborhood is sick, courting, or apologizing
bloom-and-doom.neglect: a slow day means a thin bucket and the regulars learn to check the stems before they check the price — nobody is owed a bouquet

golden-hour.ask: The folding table — Thursday evenings the big table by the dryers is folding-and-talk territory; bring your basket, the attendant puts the radio on the good station, and nobody has to talk if they don't want to.

cost.bring: laundry — that's the cover charge

golden-hour.since: since the attendant noticed the same six people doing laundry separately on Thursdays and pushed the table into the light
golden-hour.changes: a folding-table Thursday turns a chore into the hour some people see other humans — the table makes acquaintances out of parallel lives
golden-hour.neglect: the table goes back to folding-in-silence when nobody claims it — the radio still plays, the chairs still face the dryers

dusty-spine.ask: The mending night — first Sunday the back table is set with glue, tape, and cloth; bring the battered book, the shop supplies the repair kit, and your book goes home re-readable.

cost.bring: the book that's losing its spine — literally or otherwise

dusty-spine.capacity: the table fits four menders and a kettle
dusty-spine.since: since a customer tried to buy a replacement for a book that just needed glue and the owner took it personally
dusty-spine.changes: a mending regular learns the cobbler's-stitch and starts rescuing the withdrawn-shelf finds — competence the shelf silently accumulates
dusty-spine.neglect: the kit sits in its cigar box when the first Sunday passes quietly — the glue doesn't dry out, it just waits

marooned.ask: The listening station — bring a record you found or one you made; the weekend counter puts the B-side on the shop deck if it's not terrible, and the honest verdict is part of the deal.

cost.time: a side, maybe just a track
cost.bring: a record and a thick skin

marooned.capacity: the deck plays one thing at a time — the shop's ears are the bottleneck
marooned.cadence: weekends, when the counter feels like it
marooned.since: since a kid's demo got played between the trade-ins and three people asked what it was
marooned.changes: a played record makes its maker a name the shop repeats — the counter's verdict is the closest thing the block has to radio
marooned.neglect: the deck plays the same twenty records for a month when nobody brings anything — the offer lives or dies on what walks in the door

the-musket.ask: The first-Monday jam — the back room's open for whoever brings an instrument; the drummer owns the kit so drummers negotiate with her, everyone else just plugs in or doesn't.

cost.bring: an instrument, or a voice, or honest listening

the-musket.capacity: the back room holds eight players before it's a wall of noise
the-musket.since: since the house band broke up and the room felt wrong empty on Mondays
the-musket.changes: a jam regular ends up in somebody's Sunday-afternoon practice — the back room is where the block's half-bands find each other
the-musket.neglect: the back room stays dark some first Mondays — the regulars shrug and play darts, and the sign stays up anyway

bld-g9418.ask: The back garden — the shared bed behind the duplex has one unclaimed plot; take it, weed the common path when you're down there, and the herbs by the gate are anyone's.

cost.bring: seeds and your own trowel — Carmen lends nothing she can't see returned

bld-g9418.capacity: one unclaimed bed — the rest are spoken for
bld-g9418.cadence: standing; the bed's been open since spring
bld-g9418.since: since the last tenant in B left and Carmen has been keeping the bed from going to thistle out of spite
bld-g9418.changes: a claimed bed makes a neighbor into a Sunday-morning presence Carmen waters around — shared dirt is the strongest glue this building has
bld-g9418.neglect: the bed goes to thistle and Carmen keeps it barely alive anyway — an empty garden bed in a shared yard is a visible unanswered question

bld-g9457.ask: The stairwell shelf — the wide landing between floors holds a leave-a-book shelf; Unit 1 dusts it, everyone pretends not to know who, and the shelf has never once been empty.

cost.bring: a book you'd hand to a neighbor

bld-g9457.capacity: one shelf — overflow migrates to the radiator cover, which Unit 1 tolerates
bld-g9457.since: since someone left a box of mysteries on the landing with a FREE sign and the shelf organized itself around the box
bld-g9457.changes: the shelf is the building's lowest-tech introduction service — a bookmarked spine tells you who upstairs reads what
bld-g9457.neglect: the shelf accrues water-damaged romances and old manuals until someone silently weeds it — it has never once gone fully empty

bld-g9457.ask: The landing chairs — two folding chairs live on the wide landing; whoever's home and restless sits, and whoever joins shares the radiator warmth and whatever's cooking upstairs.

cost.bring: nothing — company is the point

bld-g9457.capacity: two chairs; a third gets borrowed from Unit 3's stack
bld-g9457.since: since the radiator on the landing turned out to be the warmest seat in the building
bld-g9457.changes: a landing evening is how the ambient household in Unit 1 stops being mailbox names — the chairs are the only place the floors actually meet
bld-g9457.neglect: the chairs stay folded against the wall during the busy months — the landing is just a landing until someone sits

bld-c9127.ask: The laundry line — the backyard line is shared by the four studios; the clothespin jar lives on Unit C's sill, take what you need, and Marisol's only rule is sheets off before dark.

cost.bring: your own detergent; the pins are communal

bld-c9127.capacity: two lines — whoever hangs first gets the sun side
bld-c9127.cadence: dry days, which is most of them
bld-c9127.since: since the dryer in the basement died and the landlord priced the repair against a clothesline
bld-c9127.changes: line neighbors learn each other's laundry day and start moving each other's sheets off the line when fog rolls in — the smallest reliable kindness in the building
bld-c9127.neglect: the jar goes missing for a week and everyone buys a pack at Malik's — the line works anyway, just more alone

bld-g9263.ask: The dinner-night seat — the flat's rotating dinner night technically seats whoever's around; a neighbor on the stairs at the right hour has gotten fed more than once, and the rice cooker makes eight whether it means to or not.

cost.time: a dinner that starts as lunch
cost.bring: nothing twice in a row — the house notices, kindly

bld-g9263.capacity: the table plus the couch plus the floor — the flat absorbs people
bld-g9263.since: since the cousins' first Sunday in the flat fed seven people who only meant to drop something off
bld-g9263.changes: a seat at the dinner rotation makes a stair-neighbor into family-adjacent — the flat's guest list grows by appetite, not invitation
bld-g9263.neglect: the rotation skips when all three adults pull the same rough week — the rice cooker stays small and the flat eats separately, which nobody says out loud

bld-f9344.ask: The roof table — the roof has a salvaged table and two chairs Tomás dragged up; whoever claims the evening first gets it, and the unwritten rule is you bring the table back under the awning if fog's coming.

cost.time: an evening; the stairs are the toll
cost.bring: your own everything — the roof provides view and table only

bld-f9344.capacity: the table, two chairs, and standing room for the view
bld-f9344.since: since Tomás found the table on the curb and decided the roof was wasted on the pigeons
bld-f9344.changes: a claimed roof evening is how a studio renter gets a dinner-party venue for free — the table has hosted more birthdays than the building knows
bld-f9344.neglect: the table sits under the awning through the wet months — first good evening of spring, somebody always remembers it

bld-m9102.ask: The borrowed-door table — when Victor's table (a door on sawhorses, going on twenty years) gets set up, word travels by phone and staircase; showing up with bread or a bottle is the whole etiquette.

cost.bring: bread, a bottle, or a story — one of the three

bld-m9102.capacity: the door seats ten if nobody minds elbows
bld-m9102.cadence: a few times a year, announced by phone tree
bld-m9102.since: since the shop's first Thanksgiving over the storefront, when the door came off the hinges and became furniture
bld-m9102.changes: a seat at the door-table is the strongest belonging signal on the block — it's how the neighborhood learns it has decided to keep someone
bld-m9102.neglect: the door stays a door most of the year — the dinners happen when they happen and the phone tree does all the announcing there is

bld-s9641.ask: The front steps — two folding chairs and the building's front steps; Bex sits out on dry evenings and whoever joins gets an honest opinion on whatever they're carrying, wearing, or thinking about.

cost.bring: nothing — but Bex will ask what you're working on

bld-s9641.capacity: two chairs and four steps of sitting room
bld-s9641.since: since Bex moved in and decided a stoop you can't sit on is a stoop wasted
bld-s9641.changes: a steps regular gets the sharpest honest read on the block — Bex's stoop is where half-formed ideas go to get told the truth
bld-s9641.neglect: the chairs stay inside on wet weeks — the steps are just steps and the building loses its easiest conversation

bld-d9388.ask: The parcel shelf — the lobby shelf by the mailboxes holds signed-for packages for whichever neighbor isn't home; Esther's usually there to sign, and the shelf's only rule is you take the shift when you're the one who's home.

cost.time: the odd afternoon of being home when the truck comes
cost.bring: a signature and the decency to reciprocate

bld-d9388.capacity: one shelf — it has never held more than three parcels
bld-d9388.since: since Esther retired and the building discovered it had accidentally acquired a doorman
bld-d9388.changes: the shelf makes the building run on reciprocity — the neighbor who signs today is owed a signature tomorrow, and the shelf keeps quiet count
bld-d9388.neglect: the shelf sits empty when Esther travels — parcels go back to the depot and the building remembers what she does for them

bld-sv9519.ask: The hall vacuum — the closet off the hall holds the building's shared vacuum and the masking-tape sign-out; borrow it, write your unit on the tape, return it emptied.

cost.time: the twenty minutes a studio floor takes
cost.bring: nothing — emptying it before return is the whole rule

bld-sv9519.capacity: one vacuum, four studios, no conflicts yet
bld-sv9519.since: since Asha arrived and asked where the vacuum was and learned there wasn't one — so she bought the secondhand one and put it in the closet
bld-sv9519.changes: a vacuum with four units' tape on it is a building that shares — the sign-out strip is a small ledger of who takes care of things
bld-sv9519.neglect: the vacuum sits unused the weeks everyone's busy — the tape peels and the closet is just a closet again

rules: conditions, never scripts — uptake belongs to the characters; an offer may be claimed, renegotiated, or ignored, and nothing obliges anyone to show
ignored is honest texture — neglect describes the decay state (blank lines, dust, an empty jar); nobody tracks attendance and nothing flags a cold offer for rescue
the host keeps the offer legible — a person host may let it lapse; 'staff', 'house', and 'regulars' mean no single keeper is on the hook
no promises — the changes line is the readable consequence if taken up, never a scripted outcome; a missed shared meal belongs to the characters' memory, not this file
dollars is the only money field — a numeric game-dollar cost, small by definition; no credit figures, no prices in prose, ever

keys ⊆ door venues (anchor|street tier) ∪ registry building ids; every door and every building carries ≥1 offer; offstage and reserved names key nothing but may host nothing either — they have no door
person hosts use bare ids (c1–c8, s1–s3, a01–a20); quiet rows are household/handshake knowledge and redact below internal clearance, same rule as secret web edges and quiet favors
